chunks: Ibn Mahbub from Abu Jabalah from Sa'd al-Iskaf from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

The Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) passed by some food in the market of Medina and said to its owner, 'I do not see your food except as being good.' He asked about its price, and God revealed to him, 'That he should put his hand into the food.' So he did, and brought out food that was spoiled. He then said to the owner, 'I do not see you except that you have gathered deception and fraud against the Muslims.'
ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic ruling on hiding defects in goods sold in the market?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* illustrates the Prophet’s (SAW) active role in market supervision (*hisbah*), demonstrating that divine revelation could guide specific commercial inspections to ensure fairness. By physically testing the food, he exposed the merchant's practice of concealing defects (*ghish*) beneath good quality, a key concept in Shia jurisprudence regarding valid sales contracts. This incident underscores the spiritual and legal weight of honesty in trade, linking physical inspection to moral integrity.
